Genomics & Informatics (2026) 24:19 1 Introduction Nephropathia epidemica (NE) is attributed to Puumala virus (PUUV), a naturally occurring form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in humans, which is a zoonotic infectious disease and generally considered a mild-to-moderate form of hantavirus infection within the HFRS spectrum [1–4]. PUUV (Puumala orthohantavi- rus) is classified within the genus Orthohantavirus, fam- ily Hantaviridae, and order Bunyavirales, as defined by current ICTV taxonomy, and it was previously grouped under the family Bunyaviridae prior to taxonomic reclas- sification [5, 6]. PUUV infection presents with highly variable out- comes, ranging from subclinical cases (70–80%) to severe HFRS, and carries a fatality rate of about 0.1% [7]. PUUV infection commonly presents with sudden fever, head- ache, back pain, nausea, gastrointestinal symptoms, thrombocytopenia, hematuria, and varying degrees of acute kidney impairment [1, 8]. In some patients, addi- tional manifestations such as blurred vision, dizziness, insomnia, respiratory complications, oliguria, and sub- sequent polyuria during recovery may also occur [2, 9]. Although PUUV infection is generally considered mild, severe complications can occur in a subset of patients, including acute kidney failure, hypotension, shock, pul- monary edema, Guillain-Barré syndrome, respiratory distress, disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC), myocarditis, encephalitis, pituitary hemorrhage, seizures, and, in rare cases, multiorgan failure or fatal cerebral hemorrhage [2, 3, 10, 11]. The first identification of PUUV occurred in the early 1980s when the virus was isolated from bank voles (Myodes glareolus) in the Puumala region of Finland [2]. Between July 1989 and June 1996, Finland reported 6701 PUUV infection cases confirmed via serologi- cal assays, with the highest incidence in the Itä-Savo district and a mortality rate below 0.1%, and later from 1995 to 2008, 22,681 cases were recorded with an average annual incidence of 31 per 100,000 population, resulting in 13 deaths and 52% of patients requiring hospitaliza- tion [12, 13]. PUUV accounts for approximately 93% of all notified hantavirus infections in Germany and caused a major outbreak in 2007 in Baden-Württemberg with 1089 reported human cases, while the highest annual number of PUUV infections in Germany was recorded in 2010 since hantavirus surveillance began in 2001 [14, 15]. Also in 2007, Sweden’s Västerbotten County experi- enced a surprisingly severe outbreak of PUUV infection, with NE rates hitting 313 cases per 100,000 residents [16, 17]. Between 2001 and 2017, a total of 12,148 hantavirus disease cases were recorded, of which 9714 (approxi- mately 97.41%) were attributed to PUUV infection [18]. In 2019, Europe recorded over 4000 hantavirus cases (0.8 per 100,000), 98% caused by PUUV, with Finland and Germany making up 69% of the total [19]. From 2018 to 2025, Hungary recorded 51 lab-confirmed hantavirus infections, 20 of which were specifically linked to the PUUV [20]. In Finland, between 560 and 3800 cases of NE are reported each year, though the actual number is believed to be nearly six times higher [21]. PUUV is a spherical enveloped pathogen character- ized by a segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome [5, 21]. The PUUV possesses a tripartite genome: the L segment (~ 6.5 kb) encodes a ~ 2156-amino-acid L protein (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with replicase, transcriptase, and endo- nuclease functions; the M segment (~ 3.7 kb) encodes a ~ 1148-amino-acid glycoprotein precursor that is co- translationally cleaved into Gn (70 kDa) and Gc (55 kDa); and the S segment (~ 1.8 kb) encodes a ~ 433-amino-acid nucleocapsid (N) protein [2, 5, 22, 23]. Gc is the protein that mediates fusion by the identification of a peptide of fusion, whereas Gn serves as a folding chaperone for Gc and controls the time of fusion; both are necessary for the virus to adhere as well as enter host cells [2, 24]. Gn and Gc form the principal antigenic surface of PUUV and are major targets of neutralizing antibodies, contributing to protective immunity and vaccine relevance [25–27]. The N protein plays multiple roles in viral genome transport, replication, and assembly through its interactions with host cellular proteins, while also acting as a highly immu- nogenic viral component in both humans and animal models [28, 29]. The N protein is highly conserved among orthohantaviruses and elicits a strong early antibody response during acute infection, making it an important target for both diagnostic applications and vaccine devel- opment [30, 31]. Various vaccine platforms are available, each possess- ing distinct advantages and drawbacks. For example, live attenuated vaccines trigger strong, long-lasting immu- nity but can be risky for immunocompromised individu- als due to possible reversion to virulence; inactivated vaccines are safer and more stable, though they usually require multiple doses; subunit vaccines use only key antigens, lowering the chance of side effects, but often need adjuvants and booster shots to achieve durable pro- tection [32–35]. Moreover, DNA vaccines offer rapid, stable, and cost-effective production with long-lasting immunity, but they often show weak immunogenicity in humans and face delivery challenges [34, 36]. In con- trast, the key advantage of mRNA vaccines lies in their rapid design and production, enabling swift responses to emerging infections and pandemic threats without the need to culture live pathogens [37, 38]. In recognition of these advances, the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honored Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman Page 3 of 26 Hossain et al. Genomics & Informatics (2026) 24:19 for their groundbreaking contributions to nucleoside engineering, a key innovation that enabled the successful development of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 [39]. Recent developments in bioinformatics have improved biopharmaceutical design by enabling rapid prediction of protein features, structural modeling, and immuno- genicity assessment. These computational approaches accelerate the identification and optimization of thera- peutic candidates while reducing time and experimental costs; however, challenges related to prediction accuracy, biological complexity, and the need for experimental validation remain important considerations [40]. Reverse vaccinology (RV) applies bioinformatics and immuno- informatics to screen microbial genomes for conserved, immunogenic epitopes, enabling faster, safer, and cost- effective vaccine development compared to traditional pathogen culturing, a slow and labor-intensive process [41, 42]. Vaccine development against PUUV infection has included inactivated whole-virus vaccines, recom- binant subunit vaccines, virus-like particle (VLP)-based approaches, and DNA vaccines [43–45]. Among these, inactivated and DNA vaccine candidates have demon- strated promising immunogenicity in preclinical studies [44–46]. Currently, no vaccine has been authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for PUUV infection [9, 47]. Several studies have suggested the potential of multi- epitope vaccine approaches using immunoinformatics- based strategies. Khan et al. developed a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against SARS-CoV-2 by integrating epitope prediction, antigenicity assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response analysis, demonstrating the feasibility of com- putational vaccine design approaches [48]. Similarly, Peele et al. designed a multi-epitope vaccine construct containing predicted B-cell and T-cell epitopes and evaluated its structural and immunological proper- ties through computational analyses [49]. These studies highlighted the potential of combining multiple immune targets within a single vaccine construct; however, their findings remained primarily dependent on computa- tional predictions and required experimental validation to confirm immunogenicity and protective efficacy. However, despite these advances, several challenges remain in current multi-epitope vaccine development strategies. Computational vaccine designs are depend- ent on prediction algorithms, reference databases, structural modeling assumptions, and available biologi- cal information, which may influence the reliability of predicted vaccine candidates. In addition, variations in epitope selection criteria, antigen conservation analysis, population coverage evaluation, and structural validation approaches can affect the effectiveness of computational vaccine design. Recent studies have emphasized that although immunoinformatics approaches accelerate multi-epitope vaccine development, comprehensive experimental validation remains essential for confirming biological relevance and protective potential [50]. Despite previous vaccine development efforts, includ- ing inactivated whole-virus vaccines, recombinant subu- nit vaccines, virus-like particle (VLP)-based approaches, and DNA vaccine candidates, no PUUV vaccine has currently received regulatory approval. An integrated mRNA multi-epitope vaccine strategy targeting con- served regions of both PUUV glycoproteins (Gn/Gc) and nucleocapsid protein remains insufficiently explored. A comprehensive framework combining conserved antigen identification, multi-epitope vaccine construction, struc- tural evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response prediction for PUUV has not been extensively investigated. Therefore, this study aimed to design and evaluate the PV-GNProtecta vaccine candidate using an integrated immunoinfor- matics workflow involving conserved antigen identifica- tion, epitope prediction, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and immune response prediction. The findings provide computational insights into the potential characteristics of PV-GNPro- tecta while recognizing the necessity of experimental val- idation for future assessment. 2 Materials and methods 2.1 Acquisition and characterization of viral protein sequences The UniProt protein database (https://​www.​unipr​ot.​org/; accessed on 15 July 2025) was used for obtaining amino acid sequences of the target proteins from PUUV of G (accession number: P41266) and N (accession numbers: P41270) [51]. The G and N proteins were selected due to their key roles in PUUV infection and immune recogni- tion. The G protein mediates viral attachment and entry and is a major target of neutralizing antibodies, whereas the highly conserved N protein contributes to viral repli- cation and induces strong immune responses. Compared with the intracellular RdRp/L protein, G and N provide more suitable targets for antibody and cellular immune responses. A comparative evaluation of these proteins is provided in Supplementary Table S14. 2.2 Physicochemical and structural characterization of selected proteins The selected PUUV G and N proteins were character- ized for signal peptide presence, transmembrane regions, and subcellular localization. Signal peptide predic- tion was performed using SignalP 6.0 (https://​servi​ces.​ healt​htech.​dtu.​dk/​servi​ces/​Signa​lP-6.​0/; accessed on 15 Page 4 of 26 Hossain et al. Genomics & Informatics (2026) 24:19 September 2026) with the organism group selected as Eukarya and the default prediction model [52]. Trans- membrane topology was predicted using DeepTMHMM version 1.0.57 (accessed on 15 September 2026) using the default settings [53]. Subcellular localization informa- tion was obtained from UniProt (https://​www.​unipr​ot.​ org/; accessed on 15 September 2026) based on available curated annotations [54]. 2.3 Analysis of multiple sequence alignment and evolutionary relationships To support RV analysis, the sequence is encoded using amino acid residue codes and preserved as a FASTA sequence file. The acquired sequences were subsequently utilized for multiple sequence alignment (MSA) through the Clustal Omega platform (https://​www.​ebi.​ac.​uk/​ jdisp​atcher/​msa/​clust​alo; accessed on 05 August 2025) [55]. The Mega X tool (https://​www.​megas​oftwa​re.​net/; accessed on 05 August 2025) was employed for phyloge- netic analysis on both genomes [56]. 2.4 Prediction of epitopes for MHC I, MHC II, and linear B‐cell interactions The MHC I epitopes from the G and N proteins were found using the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) (http://​tools.​iedb.​org/​mhci/; accessed on 20 August 2025) software, with a percentile rank < 1.00 as the selec- tion criterion [57]. This tool is a sophisticated database comprising information on MHC molecules, T-cell and B-cell epitopes, antibodies, and MHC-binding ligands identified in humans and various animal taxonomic groups, including primates and rodents [58, 59]. A cut- off percentile rank of less than 1.00 was implemented for epitope selection, which suggests that the binding affinity was improved [37]. Lower percentile rank values indicate stronger predicted peptide–MHC binding affin- ity [60]. The IEDB (http://​tools.​iedb.​org/​mhcii/; accessed on 20 August 2025) was applied to forecast the MHC II epitopes inside the designated areas of these proteins, and peptides with percentile ranks < 1.00 were considered potential high-affinity binders and selected for further evaluation [61]. Subsequently, the human allele reference sets were employed to predict CD8 + and CD4 + bind- ing. The ABCpred tool (https://​webs.​iiitd.​edu.​in/​ragha​ va/​abcpr​ed/; accessed on 25 August 2025) was used to estimate the continuous B-cell epitopes of the selected portions of these proteins. This tool provides epitope predictions by analyzing the sequence features of the tar- get antigens [58, 62]. This program uses an affinity scale method based on a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to predict continuous B-cell epitopes [63, 64]. Additionally, the MHC-II epitopes underwent some additional analy- ses, including IL-10 (https://​webs.​iiitd.​edu.​in/​ragha​va/​ il10p​red/; accessed on 25 September 2026), IFN-gamma (https://​webs.​iiitd.​edu.​in/​ragha​va/​ifnep​itope/​predi​ct.​ php; accessed on 25 September 2026), IL-2 (https://​webs.​ iiitd.​edu.​in/​ragha​va/​il2pr​ed/; accessed on 25 September 2026) and IL-4 (https://​webs.​iiitd.​edu.​in/​ragha​va/​il4pr​ ed/​design.​php; accessed on 25 September 2026) by using the respective servers. Genomics & Informatics Design and in silico evaluation of PV‐GNProtecta: an mRNA multi‐epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis Tanvir Hossain1, Abdullah Al Mahmud1, Maisha Afrin2, Sakibur Rahman1, Shaheda Siddiqa Tahia1, Ahmad Abdullah Mahdeen3* and Md. Habib Ullah Masum4* Abstract Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population cov- erage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escheri- chia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection. Genomics & Informatics (2026) 24:19 1 Introduction Nephropathia epidemica (NE) is attributed to Puumala virus (PUUV), a naturally occurring form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in humans, which is a zoonotic infectious disease and generally considered a mild-to-moderate form of hantavirus infection within the HFRS spectrum [1–4]. PUUV (Puumala orthohantavi- rus) is classified within the genus Orthohantavirus, fam- ily Hantaviridae, and order Bunyavirales, as defined by current ICTV taxonomy, and it was previously grouped under the family Bunyaviridae prior to taxonomic reclas- sification [5, 6]. PUUV infection presents with highly variable out- comes, ranging from subclinical cases (70–80%) to severe HFRS, and carries a fatality rate of about 0.1% [7]. PUUV infection commonly presents with sudden fever, head- ache, back pain, nausea, gastrointestinal symptoms, thrombocytopenia, hematuria, and varying degrees of acute kidney impairment [1, 8]. In some patients, addi- tional manifestations such as blurred vision, dizziness, insomnia, respiratory complications, oliguria, and sub- sequent polyuria during recovery may also occur [2, 9]. Although PUUV infection is generally considered mild, severe complications can occur in a subset of patients, including acute kidney failure, hypotension, shock, pul- monary edema, Guillain-Barré syndrome, respiratory distress, disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC), myocarditis, encephalitis, pituitary hemorrhage, seizures, and, in rare cases, multiorgan failure or fatal cerebral hemorrhage [2, 3, 10, 11]. The first identification of PUUV occurred in the early 1980s when the virus was isolated from bank voles (Myodes glareolus) in the Puumala region of Finland [2]. Between July 1989 and June 1996, Finland reported 6701 PUUV infection cases confirmed via serologi- cal assays, with the highest incidence in the Itä-Savo district and a mortality rate below 0.1%, and later from 1995 to 2008, 22,681 cases were recorded with an average annual incidence of 31 per 100,000 population, resulting in 13 deaths and 52% of patients requiring hospitaliza- tion [12, 13]. PUUV accounts for approximately 93% of all notified hantavirus infections in Germany and caused a major outbreak in 2007 in Baden-Württemberg with 1089 reported human cases, while the highest annual number of PUUV infections in Germany was recorded in 2010 since hantavirus surveillance began in 2001 [14, 15]. Also in 2007, Sweden’s Västerbotten County experi- enced a surprisingly severe outbreak of PUUV infection, with NE rates hitting 313 cases per 100,000 residents [16, 17]. Between 2001 and 2017, a total of 12,148 hantavirus disease cases were recorded, of which 9714 (approxi- mately 97.41%) were attributed to PUUV infection [18]. In 2019, Europe recorded over 4000 hantavirus cases (0.8 per 100,000), 98% caused by PUUV, with Finland and Germany making up 69% of the total [19]. From 2018 to 2025, Hungary recorded 51 lab-confirmed hantavirus infections, 20 of which were specifically linked to the PUUV [20]. In Finland, between 560 and 3800 cases of NE are reported each year, though the actual number is believed to be nearly six times higher [21]. PUUV is a spherical enveloped pathogen character- ized by a segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome [5, 21]. The PUUV possesses a tripartite genome: the L segment (~ 6.5 kb) encodes a ~ 2156-amino-acid L protein (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with replicase, transcriptase, and endo- nuclease functions; the M segment (~ 3.7 kb) encodes a ~ 1148-amino-acid glycoprotein precursor that is co- translationally cleaved into Gn (70 kDa) and Gc (55 kDa); and the S segment (~ 1.8 kb) encodes a ~ 433-amino-acid nucleocapsid (N) protein [2, 5, 22, 23]. Gc is the protein that mediates fusion by the identification of a peptide of fusion, whereas Gn serves as a folding chaperone for Gc and controls the time of fusion; both are necessary for the virus to adhere as well as enter host cells [2, 24]. Gn and Gc form the principal antigenic surface of PUUV and are major targets of neutralizing antibodies, contributing to protective immunity and vaccine relevance [25–27]. The N protein plays multiple roles in viral genome transport, replication, and assembly through its interactions with host cellular proteins, while also acting as a highly immu- nogenic viral component in both humans and animal models [28, 29]. analysis.background: Puumala virus (PUUV) is the main cause of nephropathia epidemica, a zoonotic disease with renal complications and no approved vaccine, representing a notable public‑health threat.
analysis.methods: An immunoinformatics pipeline was used to design an mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine (PV‑GNProtecta) from conserved glycoprotein and nucleoprotein regions, selecting highly antigenic, non‑allergenic, non‑toxic T‑ and B‑cell epitopes, adding adjuvants, and performing population‑coverage, physicochemical, and codon‑optimization analyses; structural models were validated (95.5% Ramachandran favored, ERRAT 91.4), docked to TLR4 with MM‑GBSA, and subjected to a 100 ns molecular‑dynamics simulation; immune‑simulation predicted IgG, IFN‑γ and IL‑2 responses.
analysis.results: The vaccine construct showed favorable antigenicity, stability, solubility and non‑toxicity, broad HLA coverage, high‑quality structural validation, strong predicted binding to TLR4, stable dynamics over 100 ns, compatible codon usage for E. coli expression, and simulated humoral and cellular immune responses.
analysis.contribution: The study provides a fully in‑silico designed mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine candidate and a reproducible computational workflow that may guide experimental development against PUUV infection.
analysis.limitations: Findings are limited to computational predictions; experimental validation of translational efficiency, stability, immunogenicity and safety is required.

analysis.summary_en: Background: PUUV causes nephropathia epidemica and lacks an approved vaccine, posing a public‑health risk. Methods: An immunoinformatics approach designed an mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine using conserved viral proteins, evaluated epitopes, population coverage, physicochemical traits, structural quality, TLR4 docking, MD simulation, codon optimization, and immune simulation. Results: The construct is highly antigenic, non‑allergenic, stable, shows broad HLA coverage, 95.5% Ramachandran‑favored residues, ERRAT 91.4, strong TLR4 binding, stable 100 ns dynamics, and predicts IgG, IFN‑γ, IL‑2 responses. Contribution: Offers a computationally validated vaccine candidate and workflow for PUUV. Limitations: Only in‑silico data; experimental testing is needed.

analysis_zh.background: 普马拉病毒(普马拉病毒)是肾病流行性(nephropathia epidemica)的主要致病因子,这是一种伴有肾脏并发症的动物源性疾病,且尚无获批疫苗,构成显著的公共卫生威胁。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用免疫信息学工作流从保守的糖蛋白和核蛋白区段设计了mRNA多表位疫苗(PV‐GNProtecta),筛选出高抗原性、无致敏性、无毒性的T细胞和B细胞表位,加入佐剂,并进行人群覆盖率、理化性质及密码子优化分析;结构模型经验证(Ramachandran受限区95.5%,ERRAT 91.4),通过MM‐GBSA对接TLR4,并进行100 ns分子动力学模拟;免疫模拟预测产生IgG、IFN‐γ和IL‐2应答。
analysis_zh.results: 该疫苗构建体表现出良好的抗原性、稳定性、可溶性和无毒性,覆盖广泛的HLA等位基因,结构验证质量高,预测与TLR4结合力强,100 ns模拟显示动力学稳定,密码子使用适合大肠杆菌表达,并在模拟中诱导体液和细胞免疫应答。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究提供了一个完全基于计算设计的mRNA多表位疫苗候选物以及可复现的计算工作流,可为针对普马拉病毒感染的实验研发提供指导。
analysis_zh.limitations: 研究结果仅限于计算预测;需进行实验验证以确认翻译效率、稳定性、免疫原性和安全性。

papers.title: DNA and mRNA Vaccines Against Hantaviruses: Antigen Design, Delivery Strategies and Translational Progress.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are members of the Hantaviridae family, which can cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). At present, no specific antiviral treatment is available for hantavirus infection, while licensed hantavirus vaccines are restricted to a limited number of countries in Asia. This review summarizes recent advances in hantavirus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines, focusing on antigen design, delivery systems, immunogenicity, safety and translational development. Peer-reviewed studies published primarily within the past 10 years were evaluated together with available hantavirus vaccine trials registered in ClinicalTrials.gov, with emphasis on Hantaan virus (HTNV), Puumala virus (PUUV) and Andes virus (ANDV). DNA vaccine candidates have demonstrated immunogenicity in preclinical and early clinical studies, with an acceptable safety profile. mRNA vaccines represent a newer approach with promising preclinical evidence of humoral and cellular immune responses. However, they have not yet been evaluated clinically. Studies have also reported the potential for varying degrees of cross-protection between hantavirus species, although protection remains limited by antigenic diversity. Overall, current evidence supports further development of nucleic acid-based hantavirus vaccines, particularly multivalent strategies, with emphasis on standardized evaluation and clinical efficacy.

papers.title_zh: DNA和mRNA疫苗针对汉坦病毒:抗原设计、递送策略与转化进展

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒es 引起 肾综合征出血热 和 汉坦病毒心肺综合征,但目前尚无特异性抗病毒药物,且获批疫苗仅限于少数亚洲国家。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述聚焦于 DNA 与 mRNA 疫苗的设计、递送系统、免疫原性、安全性以及针对 汉坦病毒es 的转化发展。
analysis_zh.current_state: DNA 疫苗候选者已在临床前和早期临床研究中显示出免疫原性和可接受的安全性;mRNA 疫苗在临床前模型中诱导强烈的体液和细胞免疫反应,但尚未进入临床试验。
analysis_zh.gaps: mRNA 疫苗的临床评估缺乏,跨物种保护仍受抗原多样性的限制。
analysis_zh.future_research: 未来工作应追求多价核酸疫苗策略,标准化临床前和临床评估,并开展疗效试验以确立临床保护。

papers.title: Epidemiology and Economic Burden of Puumala Virus Infection in Styria, Austria, 2003 to 2024.
papers.abstract: Background Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and impose a potential burden on healthcare systems. However, comprehensive economic data remain scarce. We quantified the inpatient economic burden of hospitalized patients with Puumala virus (PUUV) infections in Styria, Austria's primary endemic region, to identify hospitalization costs and early admission predictors of costs. Methods This retrospective cost-of-illness study analyzed 1049 serologically confirmed PUUV hospitalizations across 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria between September 2003 and March 2024. Costs were estimated using the Austrian performance-oriented hospital financing (Leistungsorientierte Krankenanstaltenfinanzierung) diagnosis-related group system, standardized to 2024-equivalent Euros using consumer price index deflation. Admission predictors of cost were assessed using multivariable γ-generalized linear modeling with multiple imputations. Temporal trends in length of stay were analyzed using weighted segmented linear regression. Results Cumulative inpatient cost was ∼€10.3 million (mean per-case: €9788) for the entire study period of 21 years. Three epidemic years (2012, 2019, and 2021) accounted for 53.6% of cases and over €5.2 million in expenditure, with peak annual costs reaching €1.93 million (0.274% of total Styrian inpatient expenditure) in 2012. Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; cost-ratio 1.024 per second, 95% CI 1.019-1.030) and older age (CR 1.004 per year, 95% CI 1.001-1.008) were independent admission-level predictors of higher cost. Median hospital length of stay declined by ∼50% over the study period. Conclusions PUUV hospitalizations impose a sharply episodic but recurrent economic burden on regional healthcare systems. Admission aPTT and age independently predicted cost, but clinical outcomes were not modeled and these variables do not constitute a triage tool. Epidemic preparedness strategies are warranted.

analysis.background: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and impose a potential burden on healthcare systems (A1); comprehensive economic data on these infections remain scarce (A2).
analysis.methods: A retrospective cost‑of‑illness study analyzed 1,049 serologically confirmed PUUV hospitalizations across 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria from Sep 2003 to Mar 2024 (A4). Costs were estimated using the Austrian performance‑oriented hospital financing DRG system and standardized to 2024‑equivalent euros (A5). Admission‑level cost predictors were assessed with multivariable γ‑generalized linear modeling and multiple imputations (A6); temporal trends in length of stay were examined via weighted segmented linear regression (A7).
analysis.results: Cumulative inpatient cost was ≈€10.3 million (mean €9,788 per case) over 21 years (A8). Three epidemic years (2012, 2019, 2021) accounted for 53.6% of cases and >€5.2 million, with a peak annual cost of €1.93 million (0.274% of Styrian inpatient expenditure) in 2012 (A9). Prolonged aPTT (cost‑ratio 1.024 per second, 95 % CI 1.019‑1.030) and older age (CR 1.004 per year, 95 % CI 1.001‑1.008) independently predicted higher cost (A11). Median hospital length of stay declined ≈50 % over the period (A12).
analysis.contribution: The study quantifies the episodic yet recurrent economic burden of PUUV hospitalizations for a regional healthcare system and identifies admission‑level predictors of cost, supporting epidemic preparedness strategies (A13, A15).
analysis.limitations: Clinical outcomes were not modeled and the identified variables do not constitute a triage tool (A14); only an abstract is available, limiting detail on methods and broader context.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and may burden healthcare systems, yet economic data are scarce. Methods: A retrospective cost‑of‑illness study of 1,049 PUUV hospitalizations in Styria (2003‑2024) used Austrian DRG costing, γ‑GLM with multiple imputation for cost predictors, and segmented regression for length‑of‑stay trends. Results: Total inpatient cost was ~€10.3 M (mean €9,788 per case); three epidemic years contributed 53.6% of cases and >€5.2 M, with a peak annual cost of €1.93 M in 2012. Longer aPTT and older age independently increased cost; median stay fell ~50 % over time. Contribution: Provides the first regional quantification of PUUV economic impact and highlights cost predictors, informing preparedness. Limitations: No clinical outcome modeling, predictors not a triage tool, and only abstract data are available.

papers.title_zh: 2003至2024年奥地利施蒂利亚地区 普马拉病毒 感染的流行病学与经济负担。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒感染导致肾综合征出血热,并对医疗系统构成潜在负担 (A1);关于这些感染的全面经济数据仍然稀缺 (A2)。
analysis_zh.methods: 一项回顾性疾病成本研究分析了2003年9月至2024年3月期间奥地利斯蒂里亚州20家公立医院中1,049例血清学确诊的PUUV住院病例 (A4)。费用采用奥地利绩效导向的医院融资DRG系统估算,并标准化为2024年等值欧元 (A5)。入院层面的费用预测因子通过多变量γ广义线性模型和多重插补进行评估 (A6);住院时长的时间趋势则使用加权分段线性回归进行检验 (A7)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究量化了PUUV住院对区域医疗系统的间歇性但反复出现的经济负担,并识别了入院层面的费用预测因子,为流行病防备策略提供支持 (A13, A15)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未对临床结局进行建模,且所识别的变量并不构成分诊工具 (A14);仅有摘要可得,限制了对方法和更广泛背景的细节描述。

papers.title: Seasonal Dynamics, Host Network Structure, and Environmental Drivers of Gamasid Mite Communities on Small Mammals in a Dry-Hot Valley: A Year-Round Monitoring Study.
papers.abstract: Ectoparasitic gamasid mites on small mammals play crucial roles in transmitting zoonotic pathogens like hantaviruses associated with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). To elucidate their community, network structure, and seasonal drivers in xeric habitats, a consecutive 12-month localized survey was conducted in Waxi Village, Binchuan County, a dry-hot valley in Yunnan Province, southwest China, from November 2020 to October 2021. From 1329 captured small mammals (18 species, 89.62% rodents), 12,075 gamasid mites belonging to 33 species were identified. The community exhibited overwhelming dominance by the family Laelapidae ( C r = 99.35%) and genus Laelaps ( C r = 97.37%). Laelaps algericus , L. guizhouensis , and L. nuttalli constituted the dominant mite species (cumulative C r = 88.96%) and formed a tightly correlated core species cluster. Overall infestation prevalence ( P M ), mean intensity ( MI ), and mean abundance ( MA ) were 46.05%, 19.73 mites/host, and 9.09 mites/host, respectively. papers.title_zh: 干热谷地区小型哺乳动物伪螨群落的季节动态、宿主网络结构及环境驱动因素:全年监测研究。

analysis_zh.background: 小型哺乳动物上的外寄生性伪螨传播人畜共患病原体,如汉坦病毒es导致肾综合征出血热(肾综合征出血热)。
analysis_zh.methods: 在云南宾川县瓦西村进行连续12个月调查(2020年11月–2021年10月);捕获1,329只小型哺乳动物(18种),鉴定12,075只伪螨(33种)。
analysis_zh.results: 群落以Laelapidae(C_r = 99.35%)和属Laelaps(C_r = 97.37%)为主导;三种Laelaps物种累计C_r为88.96%。总体寄生率为46.05%,平均强度19.73只/宿主,平均丰度9.09只/宿主。宿主-伪螨双分网络显示显著嵌套性(NOD Fobs = 31.16,Z = 14.03,p_H2' = 0.599),以Rattus andamanensis、Apodemus chevrieri和Mus caroli为锚点。α多样性在11月达到峰值,4月和10月最低。NMDS(stress = 0.0048)和PERMANOVA(R2 = 0.074,p = 0.001)确认季节性变化。标准RDA表明温度为主要气候驱动因素(F = 7.205,p = 0.001;模型总解释度 = 8.2%),而偏RDA显示气候仅直接解释0.1%的方差(F = 0.662,p = 0.521)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究结果表明,该干热山谷中伪螨群落组装呈现强烈物种优势、嵌套宿主-寄生网络结构以及宿主介导的季节性动态,而非直接受气候控制。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要信息;未报告详细方法、宿主特定样本量及完整统计结果。
